title: Zakat and sadaqah
hookLine: zakat is required and measured; sadaqah is any gift, any time

lines: A SMILE. A ROCK. A YEARLY BILL.
cards: A smile at the bus stop. A rock kicked off the sidewalk so nobody trips. A bill that comes due once a year, worked out to the decimal.
Which of these is charity? According to sayings of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, all of them can be. But only one is zakat.
Two of Islam's words for giving sit side by side like two hands. One is measured, owed and dated. The other has no amount, no season and no minimum.

teach.b: First, zakat, as these past days have walked through it: a pillar, owed once wealth passes the threshold, measured by a rate, due on a yearly date, sent to the eight groups the Qur'an names.
Second, sadaqah, with no fixed amount and no fixed day.

In Sahih al-Bukhari the Prophet ﷺ says every good deed is sadaqah. Other reports fill in the list: removing something harmful from the road, a good word, and, in a report in at-Tirmidhi, smiling in your brother's face.
Third, the two overlap, and the language shows it.

The verse naming the eight groups who receive zakat, surah nine, verse sixty, actually uses sadaqat, the plural of sadaqah. Pickthall translates it simply: "The alms are only for the poor and the needy."
That verse is read as the list for zakat. So the line between the words isn't a wall: zakat is a sadaqah made obligatory and given a measure.

teach.h: NOTHING TO GIVE? STILL A WAY.
teach.b: Fourth, what if someone has nothing to give? Another report in Bukhari takes that head on. Every Muslim owes sadaqah, the Prophet ﷺ says.
The companions ask: and if a person has nothing? Then work with your hands, benefit yourself, and give. And if they can't?

teach.h: THE ALMS ARE ONLY FOR THE POOR AND THE NEEDY.
teach.b: Help someone in need. And if not that? Do good and hold back from harm; that counts as sadaqah too.
So a single day can hold two kinds of giving: a duty with a calculator, and one open all day that costs as little as a kind face.

how: Muslims pay zakat once a year on qualifying wealth, and give sadaqah whenever they choose, in money, food, help or kind words.

o: zakat is the measured duty; sadaqah is any good given freely
zakat goes to family, sadaqah goes to strangers in need
two names for exactly the same yearly payment on savings

games.q: two kinds of giving — tap the pairs.

s: reports count a good word, a smile and removing harm from the road as sadaqah.
the verse naming the eight groups for zakat uses the word sadaqat
surah 9:60: "the alms are only for the poor and the needy."
someone with nothing has no way to give sadaqah
the report in Bukhari ends with doing good and holding back from harm.

games.q: the companions hear that every Muslim owes sadaqah, and ask: what if a person has nothing? what does the report say first?
o: then they are excused from it.
work with your hands, benefit yourself, and give.
games.why: work with your hands and give. and if that fails, help someone in need, then do good and hold back from harm.

practice: Walk through the hours ahead in your mind, where you'll be, who you'll pass, who will message you, and find one place where a small gift fits: a few coins, a sincere word to someone who hears little thanks, clearing something out of a path.
Pick one and see yourself doing it. If you pray, you can ask Allah to accept it.

wordCard.voice: Zakat and sadaqah. Zakat: the required share, measured and yearly. Sadaqah: any good given freely, at any time, in any amount. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: voluntary charity, any good given freely, in any amount, at any time.

carryVoice: Your line: required and freely. One gift is counted; the other is open all day. Back tomorrow, same hill.

sources.q: The alms are only for the poor and the needy
